title: Next.js App Router Best Practices
content:
# Next.js App Router

## File Structure
- `app/` - App Router pages and layouts
- `app/layout.tsx` - Root layout (required)
- `app/page.tsx` - Home page
- `app/[slug]/page.tsx` - Dynamic routes
- `app/api/` - API routes (Route Handlers)

## Server vs Client Components
- Default: Server Components (no 'use client')
- Add 'use client' only when needed (hooks, browser APIs, event handlers)
- Keep client components small, push state down

## Data Fetching
- Fetch in Server Components directly (no useEffect)
- Use `fetch()` with automatic deduplication
- Parallel fetching: `Promise.all([fetch1(), fetch2()])`

## Caching
- `fetch()` cached by default
- Revalidate: `{ next: { revalidate: 3600 } }`
- No cache: `{ cache: 'no-store' }`

## Loading & Error States
- `loading.tsx` - Suspense boundary
- `error.tsx` - Error boundary ('use client' required)
- `not-found.tsx` - 404 page

## Metadata
```typescript
export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'Page Title',
  description: 'Page description'
};
```

## Server Actions
- 'use server' directive
- Form submissions without API routes
- Progressive enhancement

title: Python Project Conventions
content:
# Python Project Conventions

## Project Structure
```
project/
  src/project_name/
    __init__.py
    main.py
  tests/
    __init__.py
    test_main.py
  pyproject.toml
  README.md
```

## pyproject.toml (Modern Standard)
```toml
[project]
name = "project-name"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest", "ruff", "mypy"]
```

## Virtual Environments
```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Unix
.venv\Scripts\activate     # Windows
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Code Style
- Use ruff for linting and formatting
- Type hints on all public functions
- Docstrings: Google or NumPy style

## Testing
```bash
pytest tests/ -v
pytest --cov=src  # with coverage
```

## Common Patterns
- Entry point: `if __name__ == "__main__":`
- Logging over print: `import logging`
- Context managers for resources
- dataclasses or Pydantic for data structures

title: TypeScript Project Setup
content:
# TypeScript Project Setup

## tsconfig.json (Strict)
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "outDir": "dist",
    "rootDir": "src"
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}
```

## Project Structure
```
project/
  src/
    index.ts
    types.ts
  dist/           # compiled output
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
```

## package.json Scripts
```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc",
    "dev": "tsc --watch",
    "start": "node dist/index.js"
  }
}
```

## Type Patterns
- Prefer `interface` for objects, `type` for unions/primitives
- Use `unknown` over `any`
- Narrow types with type guards
- Export types from dedicated `types.ts`

## Best Practices
- Enable strict mode always
- Use `const` assertions for literals
- Avoid `enum`, use const objects
- Prefer `readonly` for immutable data

title: Beads Issue Tracking Workflow
content:
# Beads Issue Tracking

Use `bd` (beads) for issue tracking during development.

## Core Commands
```bash
bd ready              # Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
bd list --status=open # All open issues
bd show <id>          # Detailed issue view
bd create --title="..." --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2
bd update <id> --status=in_progress  # Claim work
bd close <id>         # Mark complete
bd sync               # Sync with git remote
```

## Priority Scale
- P0: Critical (drop everything)
- P1: High (do soon)
- P2: Medium (normal)
- P3: Low (when time permits)
- P4: Backlog

## Dependencies
```bash
bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>  # issue depends on depends-on
bd blocked                        # Show blocked issues
```

## Best Practices
- Treat issue descriptions like GitHub issues
- Include file paths, line numbers, code snippets
- Reference plan files when applicable
- File discovered issues as you work (don't forget them)
- Run `bd sync` at session end to push changes

## Workflow
```bash
bd ready                          # Find work
bd update <id> --status=in_progress
# ... do the work ...
bd close <id>
bd sync                           # Push to remote
```

title: Claude Plan Mode Instructions
content:
# Claude Plan Mode

Instructions for Claude Code when in plan mode.

## Plan Requirements
Every plan should include:
1. **High Level Requirements** - Must-haves from user, not trivial details
2. **Architecture Decisions** - Key technical choices
3. **Data Models** - Relevant schemas/types
4. **Testing Strategy** - TDD approach: test scripts, unit tests, integration tests

## Plan Structure
- First line: document work in beads (`bd` commands)
- Split work into epics, issues, handle dependencies
- Each issue description references plan filepath

## At End of Plan
Provide list of unresolved questions (if any):
- Extremely concise
- Sacrifice grammar for brevity

## Example Questions
```
- Auth: JWT or session cookies?
- DB: Postgres or SQLite?
- Cache layer needed?
```

## Key Principles
- Plans enable TDD iteration
- Test scripts validate APIs before web implementation
- Issues should be self-contained for any developer to pick up

title: Land The Plane - Session Completion Protocol
content:
# Land The Plane

Session completion protocol. Plane is NOT landed until `git push` succeeds.

## Mandatory Workflow

1. **File remaining work** - Create beads issues for follow-up
2. **Quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update issues** - Close finished work
4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** (mandatory):
```bash
git pull --rebase
# If conflicts in .beads/issues.jsonl:
#   git checkout --theirs .beads/issues.jsonl
#   bd import -i .beads/issues.jsonl
bd sync
git push          # MANDATORY
git status        # Must show "up to date with origin"
```
5. **Clean up git state**:
```bash
git stash clear
git remote prune origin
```
6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
7. **Hand off** - Provide next session prompt

## Critical Rules
- NEVER stop before `git push`
- NEVER say "ready to push when you are" - YOU push
- If push fails, resolve and retry until success
- Unpushed work breaks multi-agent coordination

## Session Summary Format
- What was completed
- Issues filed for follow-up
- Quality gates status
- Confirmation all changes pushed
- Recommended prompt for next session
